Backup & Restore

Everything below is saved in this browser only. Download a copy so a wiped cache or a new computer isn’t a total loss.

Storage in this browser

Browsers cap what one site may keep. When this fills up, tools stop being able to save — often silently — so it is worth knowing where you stand.

How should it be applied?

    Send directly to another device

    Skip the file. Pair this browser with another device over Wi-Fi — a QR code shown here and scanned there, the same way Classroom Timer’s mirror works — and send the same backup straight across the connection. Nothing is written to disk on either end. Works only when both devices can reach each other directly (the same classroom Wi-Fi or LAN); it cannot cross the open internet.

    Start a new school year

    Four steps, in order: close the site’s other tabs, save an archive of everything in this browser, check the saved file, then review and clear the student data: names, scores and photos go, the setup they sit in stays. The clear stays locked until the file on your disk has been read back and found complete, so a blocked download or a full disk cannot cost you the year.

    1. Close this site’s other tabs. A tool left open still holds this year’s names and saves them again after the clear. Close every other tab and window of this site, then check again.
    2. Save the year archive. Every saved item and every image this site keeps, in one file. It is never locked: a passphrase forgotten over the summer would lose the year.
    3. Check the saved file. The page reads the file back from your disk and checks every item, database and picture against what it saved.
    4. Review, then clear the student data. The table is exactly what the clear will do. Names, scores, logs, photos and class lists go; the setup they sit in stays: a seating chart’s desks, hall-pass destinations, behaviour tags, a lab contract’s wording, every class name. Text you typed that holds this year’s names is listed under Your choice, set to Clear. The page looks for other open tabs again before it clears.
    Runs entirely in your browser — nothing here is uploaded anywhere. A backup file is just a copy of what this browser already has stored.
